query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating an equiatomic amount of Mn into the FeCoNi high‐entropy alloy (to form FeCoNiMn) will increase the coercivity relative to the baseline disordered fcc FeCoNi alloy by reducing the stacking fault energy, thereby promoting the formation of annealing twin boundaries that enhance domain wall pinning.
generation.material_initial_state: Disordered equiatomic fcc FeCoNi high‐entropy alloy known for its high saturation magnetization but low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Replace the baseline FeCoNi composition with an equiatomic FeCoNiMn alloy, maintaining high configurational entropy (≥1.0R).
generation.conditions: Synthesis and thermal processing (e.g., controlled recrystallization or rapid thermal annealing) should ensure a single-phase, well-mixed high-entropy structure that allows for the formation of twin boundaries.
generation.structural_mediator: Increased density of twin/annealing boundaries induced by a lowered stacking fault energy.
generation.mechanism: Mn addition lowers the stacking fault energy, facilitating the formation of microstructural features (twin boundaries) during processing. These boundaries serve as effective pinning sites for domain walls, thereby enhancing coercivity even though the alloy remains overall equiatomic.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiMn alloy will display a measurable increase in coercivity relative to the pure FeCoNi baseline while retaining a reasonably high saturation magnetization, outperforming previous soft magnetic derivatives like FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic FeCoNi high‐entropy alloy without Mn addition.
generation.boundary: The effect is expected as long as the alloy remains a single-phase, high-entropy solid solution; significant phase separation or ordering that lowers the configurational entropy would be outside the intended conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and may depend on processing parameters and subtle compositional effects, and there is a potential risk that Mn addition could also alter the overall saturation magnetization.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of samples under identical conditions: one set of equiatomic FeCoNi and another set of equiatomic FeCoNiMn. Process both by the same thermal treatment to optimize twin boundary formation. Use transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to quantify twin boundary density and a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) to measure coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: Twin boundary density from TEM imaging
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the FeCoNiMn samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercivity and twin boundary density relative to the FeCoNi baseline—or if any increase in coercivity is offset by an unacceptable reduction in saturation magnetization—the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

The stacking fault energies of CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeMnNi have been measured by Zaddach et al. using the x-ray diffraction method coupled with first principle calculations, and it has been reported that CoCrFeMnNi possesses lower stacking fault energy than that of CoCrFeNi. This suggests that HEAs may form annealing twin ∑3 boundaries more easily during GBE processes. In this research, one-step recrystallization was conducted on equiatomic FeCoNi, CoCrFeNi, and CoCrFeMnNi alloys. Analysis was focused on the evolutions of GBCD in order to investigate its correlation with increasing alloying complexity from 3 to 5 elements. The present work is the first to study the effects of grain boundary engineering processes on the grain boundary evolution of high entropy alloy comparing with those of lower-order alloy systems. The underlying mechanisms of GBCD of high entropy, medium entropy, and lower entropy alloys have been discussed in this article.
